decisions.issues: Minor: Nagoji has narrow white cuffs at both wrists that could be read as wrist wraps. They are tiny at this scale. The two figures are mid-size rather than small. Everything else matches: a laterite and earth bastion seen from below and to one side, red dust, the red conch standard and the white pennant with a diagonal line crossed by a curved line, and De Lannoy in the patched white coat with pale tied hair and no hat. Nagoji has his topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, chain and shoulder cloth, with no coat. The open sky at upper left takes both captions.

Minor issues. Two lit brass oil lamps sit oddly on the foreground parapet in daylight. A plain red flag with no conch flies from a different stretch of wall, which also has a small corner turret. The musket line fires across the riders' ground while the wooden targets stand off to the upper left. The field gun's rammer man stands close beside its muzzle smoke, though not in its line of fire. The beat reads clearly: the view is from the bastion; Maravar riders with red shoulder cloths wheel in pairs between posts; bare-chested Nair musketeers in white mundu fire a volley; and a field gun recoils with white smoke. There are no coats or uniforms and no text. The clear sky band at the top holds the caption.

Minor: here the white pennant is long and swallow-tailed, while panels 1, 3 and 5 show a shorter triangle. Its device is correct: a diagonal line crossed by a curved line. There is a small cluster of distant red tile-roofed houses at the lower right. The low angle up the staff against a hard blue sky works, with the red conch standard above the pennant. There is no text, and large open sky on both sides takes the caption and the off-panel balloon.

Minor: the two men stand on the wall behind the tooth, and the staff and standard sit on the bastion point ahead of them. In 1.1 and 1.3 they stood at the staff, but the tooth's point aiming outward over the drill ground matches the 1.5 script. The troops below stand in blocks in short white jackets with cross belts, not coats. Both men are seen from behind: De Lannoy in the patched, frayed white coat with pale hair tied in a black ribbon, and Nagoji with his topknot, grey temples, gold stud, bare shoulder, shoulder cloth, thin silver chain and moustache edge. The sky band along the top holds the balloon and the caption.

Minor: the heavy chief's eyes slide toward his neighbour rather than clearly toward the far end of the hall. Everything else matches: Nagoji has the topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, grey temples, silver chain, shoulder cloth and mundu, with no coat, no knife and no bandages. De Lannoy wears the patched, frayed white coat and his pale hair is tied back. The chiefs have no turbans, lamps have open wicks, and the upper wall and ceiling are clear for both balloons.

Minor only: the seated chiefs carry no sandal-paste or ash forehead marks (2.1 asks for these, including on the heavy older chief, here at far right), and Padmini is walking with her stick rather than seated among them. Otherwise clean. Padmini matches her sheet: black hair coiled at the nape with grey threading it, a gold ear stud and chain, a cream sari with a gold border in the old drape with no blouse, and the long stick. She turns her head, unhurried, toward the older chief on the right. Nagoji and De Lannoy are correctly out of frame. Same pillared laterite hall, with open-wick brass lamps and daylight from the open side. No painted text, balloons or anachronism, and her hands are sound. The two balloons can sit on the low-detail laterite wall and ceiling at upper centre-right, clear of all faces.

Minor: on the drill ground a few men wear white headcloths, and a few muskets stand upright with no hand on them. At this distance the effect is small. The principals are correct: Nagoji has the topknot, moustache, clean chin, grey temples, small gold stud, silver chain and shoulder cloth, with no coat. De Lannoy wears the worn, patched white coat and his pale hair is tied with a black ribbon. The musketeers wear white mundu and stand in a ragged line with gaps. Dusk sky is clear for the caption and the long speech.

Minor: De Lannoy leans on the parapet, eyes on the palace roofs, instead of a clear shrug. Nagoji, arms crossed, watches him sidelong. Both men match their sheets (Nagoji: topknot, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain, no coat; De Lannoy: patched white coat with frayed cuffs). The setting matches panel 2.3, and the dusk sky is clear for both short balloons.

Minor: at this scale Nagoji's gold ear ornament reads as a tiny bead and may hang slightly. Otherwise clean. The frame is a wide 3:1 strip. Both men stand on the rampart at the left, De Lannoy laughing in the patched white coat and Nagoji in topknot, mundu and chain. Below them the Kerala tiled roofline steps down to an audience hall with the throne platform. The broad dusk sky is clear for all three speeches.

Minor issues only. Nagoji's ear stud is a small flush stud but reads pale or pearl rather than gold. There is faint stubble shading on his jaw, but the chin reads clean. On the right wall map, a few tiny scribbles near De Lannoy's shoulder (about x 0.91-0.94, y 0.31-0.36) look letter-like at high zoom but read as map hatching at print size; the second Ramayyan balloon can sit over that map. Otherwise this is on script: war hall, timber pillars, laterite walls, unlit brass lamps, Ramayyan with palm-leaf bundle and stylus between the two men leaning on a plan of a wall. Nagoji has a topknot, grey temples, mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain, no coat. De Lannoy wears the patched, frayed white coat. Clear roof and sky space at top left and top centre for the balloons.

Clean. The young bare-chested recruit in a hitched white mundu has just fired: smoke at his muzzle and a dust spurt short of and wide of the target. De Lannoy (pale hair tied back, bare-headed, worn white coat with patches and frayed cuffs, sandals) is walking toward him from behind the line, and the onlookers stand behind or beside it. The only flag is the red conch standard. There is wide sky at the top for the short 'Again.' balloon. This panel sets the recruit's look for the page: bare-chested, curly hair, white mundu with a thin red border.

Acceptable with a continuity note. The recruit wears a white upper cloth draped over both shoulders, plus leather straps, where he is bare-chested in 3.2. His face and curly hair still carry the identity, and the beat (fumbling at a brass powder horn, sweating, anxious) reads clearly. Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny gold bead set close to the lobe, acceptable as a stud. His silver chain is worn diagonally across the shoulder cloth. Nagoji has a topknot, grey temples, curled moustache and clean chin, and turns back on Kayal to call down. Kayal is a bay with black mane, tail and lower legs and no white. The firing line is seen side-on with Nagoji behind it. Open sky at the top right takes both Nagoji balloons.

Minor issues only. As in 3.1, Nagoji's ear stud reads pale or silver rather than gold. The Maravar riders wear white shoulder cloths with red waist cloths, not red shoulder cloths. The specific recruit is not singled out in the firing line. Otherwise on script: Nair musketeers in white mundu, no uniforms, fire a high volley in time over two cantering riders. De Lannoy (white coat, frayed cuffs, ribbon-tied pale hair) and Nagoji (topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, bare chest, silver chain, arms folded) stand at the left edge, beside and behind the line. Wide sky above both heads for the two balloons.

Only one candidate listed. v02 matches the beat: the boy is grinning, sweat runs down his face, and his musket is grounded with both hands folded over the muzzle. His look (bare-chested, white mundu with red border, powder horn on a strap) matches the youth in 3.2/3.3, and the firing line behind is side-on in white mundus, consistent with 3.4. The drill ground, laterite bastion, field gun, wooden targets and red conch standard match the setting. There is no painted text and no balloons. Minor issues: the boy rests his hands on the muzzle, which is unsafe handling but reads naturally. The arched whitewashed armoury at left looks faintly colonial, but it is plausible as a fort building. The open blue sky in the upper right gives clear space for the short recruit balloon and the medium caption without covering faces or hands.

Minor only. Ibrahim's ear-to-jaw scar is on the correct (anatomical left) side but reads slightly reddish rather than pale. Nagoji's inner-left-forearm scar is hidden by his crossed arms. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has the topknot, grey temples, thick moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, silver chain and no coat or knife. Ibrahim has the white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, pocketed vest and a toddy cup. Padmini has black hair with grey threads coiled at the nape, a cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse and the stick across her knees. The scene is a lamplit laterite verandah with an open-wick brass lamp, and there is no text. Lettering space: the roof rafters at upper centre for Ibrahim and the plain wall at upper right for Padmini.

Minor only. The distant fort through the gate is a small hilltop castle rather than an angled bastion point. The low table has turned legs. Nagoji's grey at the temples is heavier than first grey, but it matches the other panels. The beat is right: Revathi is reading palm leaves without looking up, the steward is beside her, the brass grain measure is at hand and Nagoji stands before her. Both characters match their sheets. There is no text, and a large clear sky at upper centre holds both balloons.

Minor only. The camera has moved to the opposite side from 4.2 (Nagoji now left, steward right). Two small distant hilltop forts show, one above the roofline and one through the gate. Revathi's braid falls on the other shoulder. The beat reads clearly: she hands a bundle to the steward without looking at it, her eyes on Nagoji, and Nagoji has crossed arms and a sceptical raised brow. He is clean-shaven with a flush gold stud. There is no text, and the upper roof and sky give room for both balloons.

The only candidate, v01, misses the script beat and the setting. Revathi has not risen. She is still seated, gripping the arm of a carved wooden chair; the prompt forbids chairs, and in 4.2 and 4.3 she sits on a mat. The steward is not shown going. Two hilltop castles appear, one above the wall and one through the gate, where there should be a single small, distant fort seen through the gate. Nagoji and Revathi otherwise match their sheets, and the sky at upper right is clear for the balloon.
decisions.correction: Revathi must be STANDING upright, fully risen from the mat, not seated and not leaning on any seat. Draw her standing beside the same low dark-wood table of tied palm-leaf bundles from the previous panels, on the woven mat, turned three-quarter away from Nagoji, her gaze going out through the open courtyard gate at the right. Draw no chair, stool, bench or other seat anywhere in the picture. The old grey-haired steward in white cloth is small in the middle distance, walking away toward a side doorway with palm-leaf bundles under his arm, his back to the viewer. Nagoji stands behind her at the left by the carved pillar, watching her; keep his look exactly as before (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain, flush gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin). Through the open gate, and ONLY through the gate, far off and small above the palm tops, show one grey fort on a low hill with a single angled bastion point toward the viewer. Do not draw a second fort or castle anywhere else in the sky. Keep the wide daylight courtyard, carved timber pillars and tiled eaves, her indigo-and-gold sari, jasmine braid, gold armlets, bead necklace and tali, and the open sky at the upper right for one balloon.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji now sits on the mat across the low table, where he stood in 4.2 to 4.4, which is plausible for a closer two-shot. A small brass lamp is lit in daylight. The beat is right: a two-shot, Revathi's hand flat on the stack of palm leaves, and she is not smiling. Both characters match their sheets; Nagoji has a clean-shaven chin and a flush gold stud. There is no text, and the sky at upper right and the wall and roof at upper left give room for three short balloons.

Acceptable and fixes every r1 failure. Varma has black hair in a knot on his left side, the namam and pearl earrings from his sheet, and gold necklaces. He holds the plain brass-buttoned coat high like a trophy. Nagoji is nearest the camera and lit, and matches his sheet: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, and the healed brand and scar on his inner left forearm with no letters. De Lannoy stands apart by the maps in his patched white coat with pale hair tied back. Nair, Maravar and Madurai officers are all present. Minor points: a small brass cross-shaped rule or instrument lies on the table; the wall lights are candle-like open flames; and Varma's back-of-shoulder bandage cannot be seen from the front. The wall maps carry plain lines and small building pictograms, with no text. The upper-left wall and ceiling band is free for the caption, and the band above Varma's head is free for his balloon.

Acceptable and fixes the r1 maker's label. The insert shows the long white European-cut coat with one column of plain polished brass buttons catching the lamplight, plain cuffs with brass cuff buttons and no label. Beside it lie the red waistcoat, folded knee breeches, white stockings and black buckled shoes. It is on the map table with open-wick brass lamps and the latticed night window. Minor: the margin of the right-hand wall map, at the frame edge, carries tiny illegible tick marks and a speck of scrawl. This is the same kind of map scribble already accepted, and it is not readable at panel size. There is no lettering in this panel.

The only candidate (v01) misses the script beat. Varma's hands are spread flat on a map; the uniform coat is nowhere in the panel, so 'one hand flat on the coat' is not shown. His hair also shows grey at the temples, which breaks the black-hair lock, and neither the side knot above his left ear nor the left-shoulder bandage is clearly visible. The hall, lamps, bare chest, necklaces, mundu and the clear upper wall space are good.
decisions.correction: The beat is Varma with one hand flat on the NEW UNIFORM COAT, not on a map. The long white European-cut coat with its column of plain brass buttons (the same coat laid out in the previous panel, with the red waistcoat beside it) lies spread across the near end of the map table. Varma's right hand presses flat on the coat's chest, fingers spread over the brass buttons, while his other hand rests on the table edge. His hair is jet BLACK with no grey at the temples, gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, and a clean cloth bandage shows at the back of his left shoulder. Keep everything else as drawn: the V13 varma-v1 face and moustache, bare chest, gold necklaces, cream mundu with gold border, and the lamplit laterite war hall with timber pillars, unlettered wall maps, brass lamps and the latticed night window. Keep the upper wall clear for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The heavy, grey older Nair captain has white ash stripes, a topknot and no coat. He leans on the table with his hand at his chin, which reads as careful and hesitant. It is the same laterite and timber hall with brass lamps, unlettered maps and the latticed window. His hands are sound and there is no text. Minor: no other officers are visible behind him, and his fist partly covers his mouth. The dark upper-centre wall and the upper-left wall give clean room for both balloons.

Acceptable and fixes the r1 failure. Varma leans over the table toward the room with both palms planted on the white brass-buttoned coat, in a wide 3:1 strip with his face in the middle band. His look matches: black hair in a side knot on his left, the namam, pearl earrings, gold necklaces, the white bandage over his left shoulder, a bare chest and a cream mundu with gold border. His hands are sound. The laterite and timber hall has open-wick brass lamps, spear racks and the latticed window. Minor points: the coat cuff has a thin gold edge line; the left wall map carries a few tiny illegible scribble labels, the kind already accepted; and the window looks out onto a lamplit fort wall. The wall and roof areas either side of his head, upper left and upper right, are clear for both balloons.

Minor only. Varma's hair knot sits on the crown and not clearly above the left ear. Everything else matches. De Lannoy has pale hair tied back with a black ribbon, a worn white coat with patched elbows and frayed cuffs, and pale hands on the map with dividers. Varma is bare-headed and bare-chested, with gold necklaces, a gold-bordered cream mundu and a white cloth on his left shoulder, and he looks toward De Lannoy. The war hall has laterite walls, a tiled roof, open-wick brass lamps and a latticed window. Hands are sound and the maps carry no text. The roof beams across the top leave room for the balloon.

Minor. The background officers have no sandal-paste or ash forehead marks. One moustached officer at left (hand on chin, thin gold chain) faintly resembles Nagoji, but he has no silver chain of office and no topknot, so he reads as a generic officer. De Lannoy matches his sheet and the bible: pale hair tied with a ribbon, bare-headed, worn white coat with elbow patches and frayed cuffs. He leans in at the table with the room's eyes on him. Only he wears a coat, the maps carry no text and the hands are sound. The roof and the upper walls (top left and top right) leave room for two balloons.

Minor. Varma's hair knot sits low at the nape, not above the left ear, so it is placed differently from 6.1. The shoulder bandage wraps the front of his left shoulder. Otherwise it matches the sheet: bare-headed and bare-chested, gold necklaces, pearl earring, gold-bordered cream mundu, leaning over the map table and pointing. The same laterite war hall as 6.1 and 6.2, with open-wick lamps and a latticed window. The maps show only lines and pictograms, no text, and the hands are sound. The roof and upper wall at right (and the upper left) leave room for two balloons.

Accepted with moderate deviations. (1) The three other officers also wear silver link chains, which weakens the script note that Nagoji is the only officer with a chain of office. He still stands out: he is centred and lit, younger, clean-shaven, with no forehead mark, while the others are grey, bearded and marked. (2) No visible first grey at Nagoji's temples. (3) His hair is a loose curly mass with a knot on the crown, not fully bound in a Kerala topknot. (4) He is centred and lit, not the figure nearest the camera; a foreground officer at the right edge is nearer. (5) The back wall reads as grey stone, not the laterite of 6.1 to 6.3. Nagoji's constants are right: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, no forehead mark, white mundu and shoulder cloth, bare arms, no coat, knife or bandages. He looks down at the coat (plain brass buttons, red waistcoat), and the older marked officers watch. Hands are sound and there is no text. Two short captions fit over the wall between the left officers' heads and Nagoji (upper left of centre) and over the roof beams at upper right.

Minor. The gaol guards wear tall boots, not buckled shoes. The frame cuts the Goa officer just below the nose, so his lips and jaw show, not a cut at the chin; his eyes are never shown, which is the key rule. The scene is in fairly full colour, but the edges bleed into a ragged stain as asked. Everything else matches: wet vaulted stone corridor; two white-coated Portuguese soldiers with red cuffs and black tricornes walking away far down it; the officer's queue under a black tricorne, gilt-laced white coat, ornate gilt buttons, red waistcoat and sword at the hip, adjusting a cuff; guards in morions, off-white shirts and buff jerkins with nothing red or blue. Keshavrao looks back: young, faint moustache, short hacked hair, grey-brown torn tunic. Nagoji is seen from behind in a torn ochre sleeveless tunic and cream dhoti, with bandaged wrists, ankle irons, bare feet and loose curly hair. Empty manacles hang from a ring in the cell, with no noose, blood or text. The stone wall above the group at upper left and centre leaves room for the caption.

Minor only. The framing is head and shoulders rather than tight on the throat and jaw. The crown is cropped at the frame top, so no topknot reads (the hair looks loose with a thin band). The faint memory-bleed stain at the panel edge is not drawn. Nagoji matches his sheet and bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold ear stud, grey at the temples, silver chain, shoulder cloth, no coat. The upper-left roof and upper-right wall are clear for the two captions.

Clean. Varma matches his sheet: sleek black hair with the side knot above the LEFT ear, namam, pearl drops, upturned moustache, bare-chested in a gold-bordered cream mundu with gold beads, and a clean cloth bandage on the LEFT shoulder. The war hall is right (laterite walls, timber pillars, latticed night window, maps with no lettering, open-wick brass lamps). Hands are sound. The upper-left wall map and the ceiling at upper right leave room for the balloon and the caption. The white coat is not on the table here, but the script does not ask for it in this panel.

Acceptable, with minor notes. The two-shot works: the folded white coat with brass buttons and red lining lies between them. Nagoji is correct: topknot, grey at the temple, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, no coat. The brand is on his LEFT forearm. Varma is correct: left side knot, namam, pearl drops. Notes: Varma's LEFT-shoulder bandage is not visible because his gold-bordered cloth covers that shoulder; he wears an upper-arm armlet; Nagoji's scar line runs a little way up the upper arm; Nagoji's gesture is a touch more animated than 'level'. The balloons can sit on the roof timbers and upper wall along the top band.

v01 (the only candidate): the foreground Nagoji is WEARING the white coat, with red collar and lining, sleeves and brass buttons. On pages 1 to 13 he wears no coat, the bible says the new coat is never worn by anyone in this room, and the script wants the coat's buttons in the foreground, not on him. The wall map at the far left edge has script-like scribbles (pseudo-text). Varma's hair is a crown topknot, not a side knot above his LEFT ear. The over-the-shoulder framing, Varma's pose and the hall all work.
decisions.correction: Nagoji is NOT wearing the coat. Seen from behind his shoulder in the near foreground, he is bare-shouldered and bare-armed, with a white shoulder cloth over a white mundu, the silver chain of office around his neck, a Kerala topknot with grey at the temples and a flush gold ear stud: no coat, no red collar, no sleeves. The new white European-cut coat lies folded on the near end of the map table in the foreground, its plain brass buttons catching the lamplight. Wall maps carry only plain unlettered lines, with no letters, words or script-like scribbles. Varma's jet-black hair is in a side knot above his LEFT ear, not a crown topknot. Keep what worked: the over-the-shoulder framing onto Varma standing across the long timber map table, bare-chested with gold bead necklaces and a cream mundu with gold border, one hand opened toward Nagoji, the lamplit laterite war hall with timber pillars, brass open-wick lamps and the latticed night window, and the clear wall and roof space above Varma for three balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Varma's hair is a crown topknot with loose curls rather than a side knot above his LEFT ear, and his shoulder bandage is not visible (the back of his shoulder is turned away). The officers are somewhat alike. The beat reads well: Varma gesturing as he addresses the room, officers with forehead marks turning for the door, and Nagoji standing still at the right as the only man with the silver chain and no forehead mark (clean-shaven chin, moustache, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot, no coat). The roof beams across the top centre give clear space for both of Varma's balloons.

Clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and bible row: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, no coat. Varma has the namam, pearl drops, his left-side knot and the bandaged left shoulder, and keeps his eyes on the folded white coat. The wall maps are plain and unlettered. The roof timbers top centre and top right give room for both balloons.

Acceptable. Varma matches his sheet and holds the plain white coat (brass buttons, red lining, no facings or stains) at arm's length with his bandaged left arm. Two small continuity drifts: an unrolled map and a brass pen-pot now sit on the table, which was bare in panel 1, and the window bars are a square grid instead of panel 1's diamond lattice. The wall maps carry no lettering. The upper-left map wall and the roof at top right are clear for both balloons.

v01 misses the beat: there is no coat; Nagoji's fingertip presses a brass counter on a map among game pieces. The reaching arm is his RIGHT arm, and the brand is on its outer forearm, not on the inner LEFT wrist. His face is sharp and in focus instead of out of focus. His hair hangs loose in curls with no Kerala topknot.
decisions.correction: Close insert at table height. The plain white European-cut coat (clean, plain white, no lace or coloured facings) lies on the timber table and fills the lower half of the frame, with one plain undecorated round brass button large and sharp in the foreground. There is no map, no counters and no game pieces. Nagoji's LEFT hand comes in from the left, turned on its edge with the thumb up so the INNER wrist faces the camera and shows the old pale puckered brand just above the wrist (no letters or numerals). His fingers have ridged nails and hover a finger's width ABOVE the button, clearly not touching it. Above and behind the hand, his face is soft and blurred out of focus: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, hair bound in a Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, white shoulder cloth, silver chain. Keep the warm brass-lamp light and dark timber background, with plain dark wall or shadow in the upper corner for one balloon.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Varma matches his sheet: namam, pearl drops, thin upturned moustache, sleek knot on his left side, bandage on his left shoulder. He sets the same plain white coat (brass buttons, turned-back cuff, red waistcoat beneath) on the near side of the table. The hall matches panels 1 and 2. Minor: two tiny, unreadable letter-like specks on the lower margin of the left wall map, at about x 0.04 to 0.12 and y 0.35 to 0.41. They are about 15 px wide and could be covered by a balloon placed over that map. The upper-left map wall and the roof timbers at top right are clear for both balloons.

Acceptable. Full-width strip: Varma stands at the latticed window at right with his back to the room and night outside, the bandage on his left shoulder. Nagoji is alone at the table on the left, bare-chested with the shoulder cloth, silver chain, topknot, grey temples, thick moustache, clean chin and gold stud, with both hands on the table over the folded white coat. Minor drifts: the walls are dull plaster instead of the red laterite of panels 1, 2 and 4. In this back view Varma's hair coil sits on his right side rather than his left, which is subtle at this scale. There are tiny unreadable specks along the bottom margin of the left wall map. The plain wall between the pillars (x 0.45 to 0.72, upper half) and the roof timbers give clear space for both balloons.

Minor only. The small pennant is drawn as a straight blue saltire rather than a diagonal crossed by a curved line. It is drawn the same way in panels 2 to 4, so the page stays consistent. De Lannoy's head is turned to profile, a glance aside rather than strictly 'not turning', but his body stays at the parapet facing out. Nagoji's left-forearm scars show as two thin crossing pale lines instead of a puckered brand patch with one long scar. They are small at reading size. The drill men are bare-chested with staves, while in panel 2 they wear white tunics and carry muskets. The sea is more prominent than 'a distant line'. Otherwise correct: Nagoji climbs the last steps with his topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain, mundu and shoulder cloth, and no coat or knife. De Lannoy wears the patched, frayed white coat and holds a brass cup. The scene is a laterite bastion at sunset with copper drill ground below, and there is ample open sky in the top left and top centre for three balloons.

Minor only. The camera is over the shoulder and slightly high, not a true low angle along the parapet. The drill men wear white tunics with red sashes and carry muskets, and two instructors wear dark blue sleeveless vests. That differs from the bare-chested men with staves in panel 1, but they are small background figures. The pennant is a straight saltire (same as the rest of the page). The beat is clear: De Lannoy turns the brass cup in freckled pale hands, eyes on the drill below, sun low behind the far hills. His coat is patched and frayed and his hair is tied with a black ribbon. Open sky to the right of his head and across the top has room for two balloons.

Minor only. Nagoji's ear studs are small round gold balls on both lobes. They are still studs, nothing hangs from them. His topknot has a thin gold band. The pennant is a straight saltire (same as the rest of the page). The beat is clear: De Lannoy laughs softly with eyes lowered, cup raised near his mouth, and Nagoji leans on the parapet at his shoulder watching him. Nagoji's thick curled moustache, clean chin, grey temples, silver chain, shoulder cloth and bare arms all match. Clean sky across the top and to the right of Nagoji's head has room for three balloons. The hands are sound.

Minor only. The pennant is a straight X (saltire) rather than a diagonal crossed by a curved line, but it matches panels 9.1 to 9.3. The cup is a straight brass beaker where the neighbouring panels show a goblet. The hair is a slightly darker ash blond than in 9.1 to 9.3. Otherwise clean. De Lannoy matches his sheet: pale hair tied back with a black ribbon, bare-headed, worn white coat patched at the elbow with frayed cuffs. He faces off-frame toward Nagoji with the sunset behind him on the same laterite bastion. There is no painted text, and the hand on the cup is sound. Open sky at upper left and upper centre-right leaves room for both balloons.

decisions.correction: Fix these points and keep everything else. 1) Add Father Duarte's secretary, the only other civilian in the yard: a young, slim Goan clerk with short curly black hair, clean-shaven, in a plain brown ankle-length coat-robe with a brown cloth sash. He clutches a closed brown leather record book to his chest with both arms. He stands alone on open red earth about ten paces behind the two men, half-turned toward them, one foot forward as if about to step in and then stopping. He must be clearly visible and not hidden by horses or soldiers. 2) The officer shouting commands must not look like Nagoji. Make him an older, heavier man with a short clipped grey moustache and short cropped hair under a plain white cloth cap. He wears a plain white coat with a red sash, no red waistcoat and no silver chain, his mouth open and his arm pointing toward the drilling squad. 3) Draw Duarte and Nagoji smaller, about two fifths of the frame height, walking side by side in the middle distance so the fort's business surrounds them. Keep what worked: the laterite star-fort walls and arched gate, the palms, the tiled-roof stables with horses, grooms watering horses at the long stone trough on the left, the field gun, the white-coated squads with muskets, and dry-season daylight on red earth. Keep Duarte in his plain black cassock with a plain black standing collar (no white at the throat) and a small cross on a thin chain. Keep Nagoji in the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain, with the Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and tiny gold ear stud.

Keshavrao exists only inside the memory stain: a faint, dark, smoky patch of black storm water behind Nagoji's shoulder on the right side. In it, one thin young hand and narrow wrist is losing its grip on the frayed end of a straight rope (no loop) and slipping into the waves. Keep Nagoji exactly as before: white coat, red waistcoat, plain brass buttons, silver chain over the coat, Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin. On his ear, only a tiny round gold stud flush on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. No sword or knife at his hip. decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) gets the beat right: Nagoji striding toward the viewer across the parade ground, with the chain, brass buttons, red waistcoat, topknot and grey temples. The brand and scar show on his left forearm, there is plenty of upper-right sky for three balloons, and the setting is correct. But his ear ornament is a stud with a gold drop hanging below it. That breaks the MUST MATCH line (tiny flush gold stud, nothing hanging from it) and the author's ear = stud decision.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament must be ONLY a tiny round gold stud pressed flush against the earlobe, with NOTHING hanging below it: no drop, no bead, no pendant, no hoop. Do not copy the hanging drop from the reference sheet. Keep everything else exactly as in the previous attempt. Nagoji strides toward the viewer, slightly left of centre, in the white coat with sleeves turned back, plain brass buttons, red waistcoat and the silver chain of office over the coat. He has a Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache and a clean-shaven chin, and the brand with the long white scar on his left forearm. Keep the same parade ground, gate, drilling squads, field gun, tiled stables and trough. Leave a wide clear band of open sky across the upper right for three speech balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) shows Duarte older and grey, bowed in a slow nod, with the cross on a chain and good open sky for balloons. But a pale cream sliver shows in the opening of his standing collar under the chin, which reads as a white Roman collar tab. That is the 19th-century anachronism the bible forbids. Minor: the background drill squads wear tricorn hats, while 20.2, 20.4 and 20.5 show bareheaded topknotted soldiers.
decisions.correction: Father Duarte's plain black standing collar is closed right up under his chin with no gap: no white, cream or linen visible at the collar opening, no Roman collar tab, no shirt or undershirt showing. The cassock is solid black from neck to hem, with only the small gold cross on its thin chain against it. Keep the rest of the previous attempt: Duarte older and greyer, gaunt and lined, grey hair swept back with loose curls, head bowed in a slow nod with eyes lowered, in the left half of the frame. Same parade ground, gate, field gun, stables and trough in dry daylight. Draw the background drill squads bareheaded with Kerala topknots in white coats and red sashes, no tricorn hats, to match the rest of the page. Keep the upper sky clear for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The two men face each other at arm's length, and Nagoji's profile holds Duarte's eyes. Nagoji: curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot, coat, waistcoat and chain. Duarte: grey, lined, ink-stained clasped hands, closed black collar, no tab. The setting matches. Minor: a brown leather belt over the waistcoat is not in the costume spec. Balloon space is moderate: a thin sky band across the top above both heads, plus sky and low-detail roof tiles at the upper right.

Acceptable. Nagoji walks away with his back to Duarte toward the drilling lines, in white coat, red waistcoat, boots, topknot and grey temples, with the moustache visible in partial profile. Duarte stands bowed in the foreground with ink-stained hands, cross and closed black collar. A secretary hurries to his side. The open sky in the upper middle gives ample room for both captions. Minor: the secretary wears a white kurta with a shoulder cloth instead of the long brown coat and record book from earlier pages, and he is drawn large rather than small. The chain of office hangs diagonally across Nagoji's back like a baldric. Duarte's face sits in the upper quarter rather than the middle half of the height, but the frame is already 3:1, so no crop is expected.

Minor only. The Prince's training tunic here is sleeveless, while 21.2 and 21.4 show a long-sleeved wrap tunic. The background firing line is a little odd, with targets set between the firers. Nagoji is on model: curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. The two Nair guards stand behind the Prince with hands at their hilts. Open sky at top left and top centre holds all three lettering areas.

Clean. This is a bust shot rather than a very tight close-up, but the flat, set expression reads well. He matches 21.1 and 21.4 (face, forehead mark, topknot, white tunic) on the same red-dust drill ground. Open sky at upper left and upper right gives room for the balloon.

Acceptable. Varma is shown as a full back with hair and an ear rather than just a shoulder, but he stays faceless, unbandaged and in white silk with a gold border. The shielding arm ends in an ambiguous rounded elbow in front of the boy. The knife hand comes in from the stain edge with no owner shown. There is no blood and no priest. The gopuram, brass oil lamps and soft memory-stain edges are correct. Pale sky and the stain margin at top centre hold the caption.

Minor. Nagoji's coat sleeves are rolled back. Besides the correct brand and scar on the left forearm, an extra faint white scar line shows on his right forearm. The bible puts the scar only on the inner LEFT forearm. His face is fully on model, with clean chin, flush stud, grey temples and topknot. The Prince's long-sleeved training tunic matches 21.2. The two-shot staging is squared up. A wide band of sky at top centre holds both balloons.

v01 dresses the Prince in the white uniform coat with a red waistcoat and brass buttons. The bible reserves that coat for page 26. On this page he wears a plain training tunic, as in 21.1, 21.2 and 21.4. The beat is also unclear: the two Nair guards from 21.1 (bare arms, white cloth, red sashes, hands at sword hilts) are not identifiable. Nagoji glances only vaguely toward the drilling sepoys rather than past the Prince at his guards.
decisions.correction: The Prince must NOT wear any coat, waistcoat or buttons. He wears only his plain white long-sleeved wrap training tunic tied with a white cloth sash at the waist, sleeves rolled to the forearm, and plain white trousers, exactly as in the previous panel. He has no silks, jewels, chain or red cloth. Place the Prince in the middle ground, half-turned, with his face in three-quarter view. A few paces behind him, near the gate in the armoury wall, clearly show his TWO Nair guards. They are bare-armed men with moustaches and topknots, in white cloth crossed over the chest, red waist sashes and sheathed swords held at the hip, hands near the hilts, standing alert. Nagoji stands in the foreground left, three-quarter to camera, his eyes and head clearly directed over the Prince's shoulder at those two guards, not at the Prince or the firing line. Keep everything else that worked: Nagoji's face, curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold ear stud, grey temples and topknot; his white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain; the red-dust drill ground below the laterite bastion with the red conch flag; morning light; and the open blue sky across the upper third, left clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the old guard has a turban and a full grey beard with a topknot showing above the turban, while the escort on page 21.1 were bare-armed Nair guards with topknots and no turbans (22.2 matches this panel, so the page is consistent with itself). One small background musketeer at the far right stands roughly in line with a neighbour's muzzle. Prince matches 21.1 (topknot, forehead mark, plain white wrap tunic with sash). No painted text. Sky and the plain wall face give clear space at the top for both balloons.

Minor: three guards walk to the gate where the script implies two, and they are turbaned, matching 22.1 but not 21.1. The Prince is in the same plain white tunic as 22.1 and looks back over his shoulder with a set jaw. The open sky at upper right is clear for the balloon.

The Prince is dressed as a small copy of Nagoji's uniform: white coat with brass buttons, red waistcoat, red cuffs, breeches and riding boots. This breaks the chapter MUST MATCH line (a plain training tunic, no coat until page 26) and the neighbouring panels 22.1, 22.2 and 22.4, which all show the tunic. The catch also does not read as 'barely': he grips the wooden sword in a firm two-handed guard pointed at Nagoji, which could read as a thrust. Nagoji himself is correct: profile, flush gold stud, clean chin, grey temples, forearm scar, and his arm thrown out.
decisions.correction: The Prince must wear the same plain training clothes as in the neighbouring panels: a loose plain white cotton tunic with sleeves rolled to the forearm, tied at the waist with a plain cloth sash, a plain white lower garment, barefoot or in plain sandals. Give him NO coat, NO red waistcoat, NO brass buttons, NO red cuffs and NO riding boots: the white coat and red waistcoat belong to Nagoji alone. Show the catch as only just made: the plain brown wooden practice sword (all wood, no metal) arrives tumbling against the Prince's chest, and he clutches it awkwardly flat against his chest with both forearms, off balance, one foot stepping back, eyes wide. He is not in a ready guard and the sword does not point at Nagoji. Keep everything else that worked: Nagoji in uniform at left in profile, his arm still extended from the toss, the tiny flush gold stud, grey temples, clean-shaven chin, the drill ground with the conch flag, and the open sky in the upper left and centre left clear for the balloon.

decisions.issues: In all three beats Nagoji's ear has a stud with a small gold drop or bead hanging below the lobe. The author has ruled out any hanging drop and asked for this to be enforced in selection. Secondary: the legs in beat 1 are a confusing tangle of three boots, and the Prince wears European riding boots and breeches, unlike the plain training dress in 22.1 and 22.2. Otherwise the strip works: sweep, sword spinning away, a dusk bow with a purple bruise (no blood), open-flame lamps and the conch flag, with sky for the caption.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament in all three beats must be one tiny flush gold stud sitting on the earlobe with NOTHING hanging from it: no drop, bead, pendant or ring below the lobe. The Prince wears the same plain white cotton training tunic with a cloth sash in all three beats, with a plain white lower garment, and is barefoot or in plain sandals: no riding boots, which belong to Nagoji. In beat one, keep the legs readable: Nagoji's sweeping boot hooks behind the Prince's ankles, and each figure shows exactly two legs, with no extra boots. Keep everything else as drawn: the three-beat strip (sweep in afternoon light, the wooden sword spinning away while the Prince sits in the dust, the dusk bow beside lit open-flame lamps with the fresh purple bruise over a faded yellow one on his forearm and no blood), Nagoji's uniform, grey temples, moustache and clean chin, the conch flag, and the open sky at the top of the beats for the caption.

decisions.issues: The script beat is wrong. Nagoji is crouched in the dirt with a drawn steel sabre, copying the Prince's pose, when he should be standing and watching. Ramayyan also crouches, so he does not read as having arrived silently at Nagoji's shoulder. The Prince holds a real steel sabre instead of the wooden practice sword. The Prince again wears a small copy of the white coat and red waistcoat, not the training tunic from 22.1, 22.2 and 22.4. Faces, Ramayyan's look (receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus) and the drill ground are otherwise good.
decisions.correction: Only the Prince is in motion. Nagoji is NOT on the ground and holds NO sword: he stands upright in uniform at the left (white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, topknot, grey temples, tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging), arms folded or hands behind his back, watching the Prince with a flat, measuring look. Ramayyan stands just behind Nagoji's shoulder, upright and still, having arrived without a sound, in plain white cloth with his palm-leaf bundle and stylus held at his chest. He does not crouch. The Prince is at centre right, red dust on his clothes, coming up from a roll onto one knee with a plain brown WOODEN practice sword held ready in guard. He wears a plain white cotton training tunic with a cloth sash and a plain white lower garment: no coat, no red waistcoat, no brass buttons, no boots. There are no steel blades anywhere in the panel. Keep the 3:1 strip, the drill ground with the targets, field gun, gate and conch flag, the dust cloud of the roll, and the open sky band across the top left and centre clear for three balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: Nagoji has a faint stubble shading on the jaw, though the chin reads clean-shaven with a flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot and the full uniform. The Rani has a small vertical forehead mark that is not on her sheet. The flag on the fort is plain red, with no conch. The beat works: the Prince with his musket at port glances sideways, Nagoji looks the same way, and the Rani stands in the shade of the armoury eaves. Clear sky in the upper left and centre takes Nagoji's balloon.

Clean. Nagoji, clean-shaven with a stud and in uniform, strides forward with his eyes on the Rani. Behind him the sweat-stained Prince drinks from a leather water skin. The red conch standard is correct. Nagoji walks toward the camera more than toward her, which still reads. The forearm scar shows reddish but is not blood. Open sky at the top left takes Nagoji's balloon, and the sky above the wall at the top centre and right takes the Rani's.

Clean. The Rani matches her sheet (severe bun, plain white with a gold border, ear studs), and her hard gaze is turned right toward the drill line where her son trains. Nagoji and the Prince are out of frame, as scripted. The large sky at the upper right holds both balloons. Nagoji is off-panel, and his tail is set to the right edge to match his position beside her in 23.4.

Clean. The Rani turns fully to face Nagoji. Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a flush gold stud, grey temples and a topknot, and wears the white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. Same drill ground and light as the earlier panels. The flag on the fort is plain red, with no conch. Open sky at the top left and top centre fits both of the Rani's balloons above her head.

Minor only: a female spear-bearer at the far left wears a similar white sari and bun. She has a different, younger face and a red sash, so she reads as an attendant rather than a second Rani. The panel is a wide strip with the Rani's hard face in the middle band. The red conch standard is correct. The firing line shoots side-on, away from the watchers, with smoke and no gore. The wide sky right of her head fits the two Rani balloons and Nagoji's off-panel line, whose tail goes to the right edge.

Minor: the 'ghost of a smile' is very faint, closer to composed neutrality. The Rani matches her sheet: severe bun, small gold ear studs, white sari with a narrow gold border. The firing line is side-on with her behind it. The conch standard is plain. There is no text, and the open sky at upper right and centre takes both balloons.

The open hand holding the coin is Nagoji's RIGHT hand in both the main picture and the inset (thumb uppermost, the arm reaching from his forward side as he faces left). The script calls for his LEFT hand. The pale healed scar is painted on the inner RIGHT wrist and forearm, with a short crossing stroke that reads like a cross in the main picture. There is no thin scar across the palm. This contradicts the script and the bible, which places the brand and long white scar on the inner LEFT forearm. Everything else works: both faces match their sheets, Nagoji has the curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, grey temples and topknot, the uniform and silver chain are correct, the coin moment and inset read clearly, and there is sky at upper left and centre for the balloons.
decisions.correction: Make the open hand Nagoji's LEFT hand in both the main picture and the inset. Keep the Senior Rani at left facing right and Nagoji at right facing her. Turn Nagoji slightly away from the camera into a three-quarter rear view over his left shoulder, his face in profile with the curled moustache and the flush gold ear stud visible, so that the arm reaching to her, nearest the camera, is his LEFT arm. His right arm stays down at his side. In the inset at lower right, his LEFT hand enters from the right edge in the white coat cuff with one plain brass button. It is palm up, fingers toward the left, thumb on the lower, near side of the hand, with the small worn gold coin resting in the palm and the fingernails ridged. The only scar is one thin pale healed line running across the palm. The wrist and forearm show no scars, lines, crosses or marks of any kind, and the cuff covers the wrist. Keep everything else as it is: the red-dust drill ground with the bastion and conch standard, both faces and costumes, the silver chain over the white coat and red waistcoat, and the open sky across the top of the frame for lettering.

decisions.issues: Minor: Nagoji holds out his right hand here. If the regenerated 24.2 uses his left hand, the coin changes hands between panels, but 24.3 does not specify a hand, so this is acceptable. The staging and room match 24.2: the Rani is at left, Nagoji at right, on the same drill ground. Both faces match their sheets. Nagoji has the moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. The hands are sound, there is no scar or text, and the large sky at upper left and centre takes both balloons.

Minor: this is a bust shot rather than a true face close-up, and her calm reads slightly stern, which suits the threat. Her face matches the sheet. Both firing lines are side-on with her behind them. The sky at upper left and upper right takes three balloons. Nagoji's line is off-panel to the right, where she is looking.

The Prince wears Nagoji's full uniform: white European coat, red waistcoat and brass buttons. The MUST MATCH line puts him in a plain training tunic on this page, with the white coat only from page 26, and page 23 shows him in a sweat-darkened cream tunic. Side by side, he reads as a miniature double of Nagoji. Nagoji and the Prince are also sitting on a crate, although the whole scene has been played standing and the script has the Prince come to Nagoji's elbow. The Senior Rani, walking away, has gained a necklace, though she should wear no ornament. Nagoji's face and identity are correct, the Rani's walk-away reads well, and there is ample sky for the balloons.
decisions.correction: The Prince wears a plain cream cotton training tunic, sweat-darkened, belted with a white cloth sash, over cream trousers and boots, as on the previous page. He has NO white coat, NO red waistcoat, no brass buttons and no jewels. The white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain belong to Nagoji alone in this panel. Both Nagoji and the Prince are STANDING on the open drill ground, with no crate, bench or seat. The Prince, about fourteen, beardless and narrow-shouldered with his small topknot, stands just at Nagoji's elbow, a head shorter. Both are turned toward the Senior Rani as she walks away. Keep the rest: the wide strip with Nagoji and the Prince at left and their faces in the middle band, Nagoji's curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold ear stud and grey temples. Keep the Senior Rani small at right walking away toward the gate, back straight, in her plain white sari with the narrow gold border and NO necklace or other ornament. Keep the laterite bastion, the conch standard and the open sky above for lettering.

decisions.issues: Only v01. The beat, mist, pre-dawn light and the Prince's smaller grey are right, and Nagoji is on model (curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, topknot, grey temples, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain). The problem is the Prince: he wears Nagoji's uniform, a white European coat with a red waistcoat and brass buttons. His MUST MATCH line, and pages 21 and 23 of the script, keep him in a plain training tunic until page 26, where 'the same white coat as the others' is the payoff. Kayal also shows a small white streak or star on her forehead, and she should have no white markings. All other page-25 panels are being regenerated with the Prince in a tunic, so accepting this frame would leave the page inconsistent.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, mist, pre-dawn lavender sky, fort, torches, the red conch standard and both horses as drawn. Change only the Prince's clothes. He wears a plain knee-length cream cotton training tunic with no collar, no buttons, no braid and no coat or waistcoat, tied at the waist with a plain cream cloth sash, with loose cream trousers and plain dark riding boots. Nothing red is on him, and he has no silks or jewels. Only Nagoji wears the white European coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Kayal's face is solid bay with no white star, blaze or streak on the forehead. Keep the Prince's mount a smaller light dapple-grey with a darker grey mane, tail and lower legs, clearly shorter than Kayal.

decisions.issues: Only v01. The sunrise gold-and-green light, the trotting side by side and Nagoji's look are all good. Three things fail. First, the Prince rides a bay that is almost a copy of Kayal, but panel 25.1 puts him on a smaller grey. Second, he turns his head up and sideways toward Nagoji, while the script says he looks straight ahead, not at Nagoji. Third, he wears Nagoji's white coat and red waistcoat instead of his plain training tunic, which the script holds back until page 26.
decisions.correction: Keep the sunrise over the tree line, the gold-and-green light, the drill ground, the fort and the clear sky in the upper part of the frame. The Prince rides a smaller light dapple-grey horse with a darker grey mane, tail and lower legs, clearly shorter than Nagoji's bay mare Kayal. His face is in three-quarter view, turned forward along his horse's line of travel, and his eyes look straight ahead between his horse's ears, never toward Nagoji. He wears a plain knee-length cream cotton training tunic with no collar, no buttons, no braid and no coat or waistcoat, tied with a plain cream cloth sash, with loose cream trousers and plain dark riding boots. Nothing red is on him. Only Nagoji wears the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The light is bright blue-sky mid-morning rather than a low gold dawn. The Prince wears the plain training tunic the bible asks for, on the grey, so he no longer matches the white coat in 25.1 and 25.2 (those panels are the ones off-bible). A parked field gun at the right points across the ground but nobody is firing it. Nagoji matches his sheet: curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, grey temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. Hands are sound, the horses face each other muzzle to muzzle, and there is no text. Open sky across the top 20 to 25 percent leaves room for all three balloons, with Nagoji's two on the left and the Prince's on the right.

Only v01. The framing, low sun behind him, face, gold stud, topknot, grey temples and uniform are good, and the sky gives ample lettering space. There are two problems. On his bare left forearm the brand is drawn as a crisp dark circled glyph, like a stamp or tattoo with an arrow-like symbol inside. It reads as a sign or letter, when it should be a pale puckered patch of ridges blurred past reading. Second, the chin and jaw carry visible stubble texture, though he should be clean-shaven.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact framing, pose, expression, the low sun behind his head, the fort, the drill-ground background and the open sky above. His white coat sleeves come down to the wrists on both arms, with the red cuffs at the wrist, so both forearms are fully covered and no brand, scar, mark or symbol shows on any skin. Draw no circle, arrow, letter, stamp or tattoo-like mark anywhere on him. His chin, jaw and cheeks are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble hatching, and only the thick curled moustache is kept.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji's topknot sits close to the top edge of the strip, but it is not cut off. Both horses face the same way rather than each other, which is fine for this beat. The Prince is in the plain tunic on the grey, matching the pick for 25.3. Gold sunrise light on the right reads as dawn. Nagoji matches his sheet: moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, grey temples, white coat, red waistcoat and chain. The Prince looks at Nagoji, hands are sound, and there is no text. Open gold sky above and between the riders, at x 0.35 to 0.85 and the top 25 percent, leaves room for the Prince's two balloons.

Minor only: the Prince kneels and holds the flask to the recruit, who is already propped in the shade of the post, so the hauling is implied, not shown. Nagoji carries a sheathed sword, which is not a knife. Everything else matches: Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a flush gold stud, grey temples and topknot, sleeves closed to the wrist with no forearm marks, and the chain over his white coat and red waistcoat. There is no lettering, and the stains on the recruit read as dust, not blood. The wall and sky strip above the two heads are clear for both balloons.

Minor only. The pennant is a straight dark-blue saltire, not a diagonal crossed by a curved line, but it matches the rest of the page. There is light stubble shading on Nagoji's jaw, though his chin reads clean-shaven. Otherwise it is clean: evening on the laterite bastion, Nagoji in the white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain with a topknot, a gold stud and grey temples, and the Prince beside him in the same white coat with his forehead mark. The open sky across the top is good for the three balloons.

Minor: this is a medium three-quarter-back shot, not a tight close-up, but the beat reads, with the Prince looking out over the drill ground and not at Nagoji. The pennant is a blue X on white rather than a diagonal crossed by a curved line, but it matches kept panel 26.2 exactly. The earlier correction is fully applied: white coat with brass buttons and a red waistcoat collar, his topknot and white forehead marks, a nearly empty ground with a few small men, and no torches. The evening gold light matches 26.2. There is plenty of open sky at top right and top left for both balloons. Nagoji's off-panel tail points to the left edge, matching his position at the Prince's right in 26.2.

Minor: the shoulder roll is subtle (his shoulders are squared and lifted). What reads strongly is the following beat: the Prince glances up at Nagoji with a small, wry, lopsided smile. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, smooth clean-shaven chin, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot, chain over the white coat and red waistcoat, and sleeves to the wrist with no brand or scar showing. The faint lines on the back of his hanging left hand read as tendons. He stands level, with one hand on the parapet. The Prince has forehead marks and a topknot as in 26.2 and 26.3. The bastion, the conch standard and the matching pennant are the same as in 26.2, with gold evening light. Hands are sound, and there is no lettering. The open sky across the top is clear for all three balloons.

Minor only. The memory stain at the right edge is soft-edged but fairly opaque rather than faint. The Prince has no forehead mark here. Nagoji's face sits in the upper quarter of the strip. Otherwise the beat is clear: the Prince walks down the bastion steps in the same white coat and red waistcoat, the turbaned guards smile and nod rather than bow, and Nagoji watches from above with a clean chin, gold stud and silver chain. The boy of ten in white stands wide-eyed in a Kerala house courtyard at the edge. The open evening sky across the top centre takes both captions without touching faces.

Minor only. Thoma is clean-chinned with a moustache, but 27.3, 27.5 and the page 28 frames give him a short black beard. The bible has no beard rule for him, so this is a consistency note, not a failure. His betel stain is light (reddish lower teeth). Caption space is the sky strip across the top (about x 0.40 to 0.78, y 0 to 0.11). It fits two medium captions above the heads. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch24 uniform row: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat and chain over the coat.

Clean. Thoma is broad, in a white tunic with a cross on a cord, and his teeth are betel-red. His right hand lies flat on a bronze gun in the same tiled-shed laterite yard as the rest of the page. The engraving on the barrel is floral, not pseudo-text. The background crew all face away. The large clear sky at upper right takes both Thoma balloons. Minor: Thoma has a full beard here, while panels 27.1 and 27.5 (v01) show a moustache with stubble. His bible row does not specify facial hair.

Clean. Nagoji matches his sheet and bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, a tiny gold stud on the lobe, Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, white coat with brass buttons, red waistcoat, the silver chain over the coat and riding boots. Thoma squints along the barrel with one hand on the wooden elevation quoin. No text, and hands and anatomy are sound. The wide sky across the top lets Nagoji's balloon sit upper left and Thoma's upper right. Thoma's beard matches 27.2 v02 but is fuller than in 27.1 and 27.5 (v01).

Clean wide shot of the gun firing. Smoke comes from the muzzle, the downrange wooden target bursts into splinters, and the slow-match man touches the vent. The rammer with the sponge and a loader holding shot stand nearby. Thoma (broad, white tunic, cross) watches at the left, hands on hips. The banners are plain cloth and nothing is painted as text. A big clear sky across the top takes the single caption. The frame is a wider 1774x887 format, and the river and hills beyond the wall go further than the palm-lined walls in 27.2 and 27.3, but it is the same tiled shed and laterite yard.

Clean. Thoma grins through the smoke with visibly betel-stained red-brown and yellow teeth. His short black beard and curly black hair match page 28.
